Independent bounded replay: for each root a and five bits b0,…,b4, fill (i,j) of the 4×4 tile with b_(2⌊i/2⌋+⌊j/2⌋) when i,j are odd; otherwise use b4 if i,j are both at least two, and a otherwise. For each wrong residue (0,1),(1,0),(1,1), mark the tile if a fully contained 2×2 square originating at that residue has sum two. This gave 64 distinct tiles and 8 of 32 marks per root for each residue.
correctness.rationale: The aligned root languages are disjoint and q_(n+1)=2q_n^4; log(2q_n)/4^n tends to (log 2)/3. Any supertile can be repeated periodically: four identical copies are allowed when the fourth child takes the same root. Every finite patch of the repetition fits in a sufficiently high tile, giving legality, density, and the entropy lower bound from actual configurations. Specifying the residue phase and the tiles meeting a window gives the matching upper bound. Periodic repetitions have compatible hierarchies with all coarse fields legal, and compactness gives fibers over all points. Conversely any coarse legal field with a compatible residual phase and arbitrary corner decoration is legal by inflating a supertile containing the required finite coarse patch. Invariant measures lift by averaging. For any finite phase resolution, the phase information on a whole window is determined by one residue, so the odometer joining adds no entropy. Rescaling by the index-four subgroup in each parity fiber gives 4h≤h_top+log 2. The Haar-phase fair-corner construction yields legal configurations: a fixed site remains inherited with probability (3/4)^n after n levels, and the probability a fixed finite window crosses a level-n boundary is O(2^−n). The coarse law is the same and is independent of the fair corner field; equality follows. In any maximizing lift a finite conditional entropy deficit relative to coarse coordinates and finite residual phase digits would recur at positive density on disjoint translates, lowering the joint entropy below equality. Thus the corner field is independent and fair at each level, and the coarse field again maximizes entropy. Iteration and the inheritance estimate fix all finite marginals. The independent phase-witness count is 8/32 per root and wrong offset; conditional on the root field, independent internal bits across level-two tiles eliminate each wrong offset almost surely. Recursing recovers the Haar phase. Its horizontal parity character changes sign, so the unique MME is not mixing.
residual_risks: The finite replay only checks level-two witnesses. Entropy, uniqueness and all phase digits use the all-level proof.

value.rationale: This simple planar hierarchy has a unique positive-entropy maximizing measure that retains a nonmixing dyadic factor despite dense periodic points. It distinguishes periodic approximation from measure mixing and gives a reproducible mechanism for almost-sure phase recovery without global recognisability. The exact combination is more informative than the supertile count or elementary entropy computation alone.
residual_risks: No universality for primitive planar rules, and no assertion that all invariant measures have the same phase factor.
